task: OpenClaw owner-gated Mac GUI screen inspection fail-fast
problem: The owner request '지금 떠 있는 쿠팡 화면에 어떤 것들이 보여?' timed out because OpenClaw routed screen reading through raw Peekaboo shell commands. The OpenClaw GUI bridge socket was missing and the local Peekaboo runtime lacked Screen Recording/Accessibility permissions, so three Peekaboo shell calls waited until the user interrupted them after about 122 seconds.

implementation.summary: Added owner-gated harness_screen_inspect routing, one-shot execution-token binding, direct-call rejection, Peekaboo shell blocking during routed screen-inspection turns, and bounded fail-fast Peekaboo bridge/permission/screen checks.
Documented the native inspect-only screen route and explicit bridge/permission blocker reporting.

Added regression coverage for screen-inspection intent detection, quoted-context isolation, owner/non-owner routing, direct-call rejection, Peekaboo shell blocking, one-shot tool-call binding, and duplicate toolCallId idempotence.

residual_risk: Actual screen contents can only be returned after the OpenClaw GUI bridge socket exists and macOS Screen Recording/Accessibility permissions are granted. The implemented fix prevents the prior 122-second hang and returns that blocker explicitly.
